programme: FOSL2, EGR1, JUND and REL are the immediate-early/AP-1-NF-κB arm (Fra-2, Egr-1, JunD, c-Rel) that a smoke/oxidative-stress signal switches on to drive a cytokine-MMP-TIMP remodeling programme (IL6, TNF, IL1B, MMP12/13/14, TIMP1, TGFB1, SERPINE1 sit in their target lists); PPARG and NR1H2 (LXR-β) are the paired lipid-sensing nuclear receptors that normally hold that same programme in check in macrophages (they co-target SREBF1 and LPL, and PPARG/LXR ligand engagement classically transrepresses AP-1/NF-κB output). The module is the pro-inflammatory/anti-inflammatory balance a macrophage runs when it is loaded with lipid and hit with oxidative stress at once.
role_in_a: In vascular/plaque macrophages and smooth muscle, this AP-1/NF-κB arm (FOSL2, EGR1, JUND, REL) is the expected driver of the cytokine and matrix-remodeling output of atherosclerotic inflammation (IL6, TNF, MMP/TIMP imbalance), while PPARG/LXR(NR1H2)-driven cholesterol efflux and lipid handling is the counter-regulatory arm that governs foam-cell formation and normally dampens that same inflammatory output — none of this is stated for CVD in the retrieved record (Open Targets shows no association for any of the twelve factors here), it is inferred from the factors' known biology.
role_in_b: In COPD this is directly evidenced: FOSL2 and EGR1 are documented smoke/mechanical-stress-induced drivers of cytokine/chemokine and remodeling gene expression in airway macrophages and bronchial epithelium (PMID 18358739, 41333036, 41615694, 41213067), REL/c-Rel is implicated as an NF-κB subunit active in COPD (PMID 40508027), JunD is linked to oxidative-stress lung injury and downregulation in diseased lung (PMID 31578304), and PPARG has multiple direct COPD associations (PMID 42432584, 42328420, 40986607).
shared_axis: Cigarette smoke is the exposure both tissues share: it drives oxidative and mechanical stress that activates the same AP-1/NF-κB module (FOSL2, EGR1, JUND, REL) in vascular and airway macrophages/epithelium, producing a convergent cytokine-MMP-TIMP remodeling signature, while the PPARG/LXR lipid-sensing arm that normally restrains this signature is engaged in both smoke-exposed alveolar macrophages and lipid-loaded plaque macrophages — this is the mechanistic core of the well-known COPD-cardiovascular comorbidity.
reasoning: The COPD side of the module is independently and repeatedly placed in the literature (FOSL2, EGR1, REL, JUND, PPARG each have a direct COPD citation), so the programme is nameable and real; but nothing in the retrieved record places any of these six factors in cardiovascular disease — Open Targets records no CVD association for any of the twelve candidate factors — so the CVD half of the story rests on the general, separately-established biology of AP-1/NF-κB and PPARG/LXR in macrophage/atherosclerosis biology rather than on anything retrieved here, which caps this at moderate rather than strong.
support: PMID 18358739 (FOSL2, cigarette-smoke-induced cytokine/chemokine expression in COPD macrophages); PMID 41333036 (EGR1 in smoke-induced pyroptosis of pulmonary epithelial cells); PMID 41615694 (EGR1-associated inflammatory/remodeling response in bronchial epithelial cells); PMID 41213067 (EGR1 among aberrant immune/transcriptional genes in single-cell COPD data); PMID 40508027 (REL/c-Rel among NF-κB subunits implicated in COPD); PMID 31578304 (JunD linked to oxidative-stress lung injury/emphysema and downregulated in diseased human lung); PMID 42432584, PMID 42328420, PMID 40986607 (PPARG associated with COPD risk/pathogenesis through three independent lines of evidence). No retrieved PMID places any of these factors in cardiovascular disease.
how_to_falsify: In parallel smoke/oxidative-stress-challenged vascular macrophages (or human plaque macrophages) and COPD airway macrophages, run ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN for FOSL2, EGR1, JUND and REL at the IL6/TNF/MMP12/MMP13/TIMP1 loci and PPARG/NR1H2 agonist treatment with the same readout: if the vascular cells fail to show the same AP-1/NF-κB occupancy and remodeling-gene induction that the COPD cells show, or if PPARG/LXR agonism fails to suppress that induction in vascular macrophages the way it is expected to in lung macrophages, the shared-axis claim is falsified.
caveats: Blood-lung tissue pairing across 104 patient-group comparisons from 4 independent cohort pairs, which is reasonable replication depth for the concordance counts (FOSL2 84/104, EGR1 79/104, PPARG/NR1H2/REL/JUND each 63-64/104). Every one of the twelve candidate factors has 'no association recorded' in Open Targets for cardiovascular disease specifically, which is a real evidentiary gap, not an oversight. Tissue-generic exclusion removed STAT1, FOS, ESR1, RELB and other classic inflammatory/interferon TFs, so the account deliberately does not lean on those. Single-view exclusions (KLF6, KLF1, SIX1, etc.) removed subgroup-specific noise. MITF, ASCL1, HOXC6, CDX1 and HES6 also met the concordance bar but are melanocyte/neuroendocrine/HOX/Notch-lineage factors with no documented tie to either disease (per the reader's notes) and no plausible role in this inflammatory/lipid axis — they are left out of the carrying set rather than forced into the story, and their presence in the concordant list is unexplained here.
